title: The Story of Ungal Nesavalan – A Tradition of Trust, Quality & Textiles
excerpt: Discover Ungal Nesavalan, where traditional textile craftsmanship meets modern fashion. Bringing you beautiful sarees, quality fabrics and timeless designs with a promise of trust, value and customer satisfaction.
content:
Welcome to Ungal Nesavalan

Every saree has a story. A story of creativity, craftsmanship, tradition and the hands that bring beautiful fabrics to life.

At Ungal Nesavalan, we believe that a saree is more than just a piece of clothing. It represents our culture, tradition, beauty and the timeless connection between generations.

Our Journey

Rooted in the textile heritage of Elampillai, Tamil Nadu, Ungal Nesavalan is dedicated to bringing beautiful sarees and quality textiles closer to every customer.

Our journey is driven by a simple vision: to make beautiful, quality sarees accessible to everyone without compromising on design, comfort or value.

From traditional silk cotton sarees to elegant soft silk collections and everyday cotton wear, we continuously explore beautiful designs to suit every occasion.

Our Love for Sarees

We understand that every customer has a different taste and every occasion deserves something special.

That's why our collections bring together:

Traditional Silk Cotton Sarees

Elegant Soft Silk Sarees

Beautiful Kanchipuram Pattern Sarees

Premium Cotton Sarees

Wedding & Festive Collections

Unique Traditional and Contemporary Designs

Every collection is selected with attention to appearance, comfort and value.

Our Commitment to Quality

Quality is not just a promise. It is the foundation of everything we do.

We believe our customers deserve products that offer beautiful designs, comfortable fabrics and excellent value for money.

We continuously strive to bring collections that make every purchase a satisfying experience.

More Than a Business – A Family

At Ungal Nesavalan, our customers are not just buyers. They are part of our growing textile family.

Your trust, support and love motivate us to bring better collections and better shopping experiences every day.

Whether you are shopping for a wedding, a festival, a special occasion or everyday elegance, we are here to help you find something beautiful.

Our Vision

Our vision is to take the beauty of Indian textiles and traditional saree collections to customers across India.

We want every customer to experience the joy of wearing beautiful sarees with confidence, comfort and pride.

Ungal Nesavalan – Your Tradition, Our Passion.

Thank you for being part of our journey.

With love,
Team Ungal Nesavalan

title: Why Kanjivaram silks are woven on pit looms
excerpt: Three feet below the floor, master weavers in Kanchipuram pedal at a rhythm passed down through nine generations. Here's what that pit does for the silk.
content:
The first thing you notice, standing next to a Kanchipuram loom, is that the weaver is sitting *below* the floor. Their legs disappear into a pit that's roughly three feet deep, and the treadles — the pedals that lift and drop the warp threads — hang from the ceiling on ropes.

This isn't nostalgia. It's physics.

## Why the pit matters

A pure zari Kanjivaram sari has three separately woven pieces: the body, the *pallu* (the decorated end that drapes over the shoulder), and the border. The three are joined with a specialised interlocking weave called *korvai* — you can hear the tiny snap of it when the sari is pulled taut. Getting korvai clean requires a very specific tension on the warp, which requires the weaver to shift their weight *downward* into the pedals rather than pressing forward. In a pit loom, gravity does most of that work.

Above ground, you can get more speed. Below ground, you get better *fall*.

## What it costs

A single Kanjivaram sari with an all-over zari body takes 15 to 25 days on a pit loom. On a mechanised jacquard, you can be through 30 saris in the same time — but the silk won't sit the same way on the body. The drop is heavier, the border sits crooked when you sit down, and after a wash the zari dulls faster because the mechanical loom pulls the metallic thread through at a harder angle.

The premium you pay for a pit-loom Kanjivaram isn't for the silk. It's for the twenty days.

## The next generation

We work with three weaver families in Kanchipuram whose youngest weaver is 34 and whose oldest is 71. When we ask what they need, the answer is never "better looms." It's always "someone who wants to buy what we already know how to make."

That's the whole idea behind Ungal Nesavalan.
